articleTitle: EmoTech: A Multi-Modal Speech Emotion Recognition Using Multi-Source Low-Level Information with Hybrid Recurrent Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Emotion recognition is a critical task in human-computer interaction, enabling more intuitive and responsive systems. This study presents a multimodal emotion recognition system that combines low-level information from audio and text, leveraging both Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Networks (BiLSTMs). The proposed system consists of two parallel networks: an Audio Block and a Text Block. Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) are extracted and processed by a BiLSTM network and a 2D convolutional network to capture low-level intrinsic and extrinsic features from speech. Simultaneously, a combined BiLSTM-CNN network extracts the low-level sequential nature of text from word embeddings corresponding to the available audio. This low-level information from both speech and text is then concatenated and processed by several fully connected layers to classify the speech emotion. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed EmoTech accurately recognizes emotions from combined audio and text inputs, achieving an overall accuracy of 84%. This solution outperforms previously proposed approaches for the same dataset and modalities.

articleTitle: Estimating Response of Fractional Order Systems and Control: An Orthogonal HF-BasedApproach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: In an attempt to simplify the mathematical solution of real-world systems, further presumptions such as an integer order system and zero initial condition lead to imprecise and incorrect system modeling. By modeling real-world systems with fractional orders these problems can be solved with more accuracy. However, analyzing those systems and determining time-based responses are quite difficult challenges. Several techniques for fractional order system approximation were developed earlier and are accessible in the literature to reduce the mathematical complexity. However, the proposed method for solving the issue is more efficient and provides far more accurate results with a simpler algorithm than existing methods. Based on the orthogonal hybrid functions (HF), the suggested method is found. When working with function samples, the orthogonal HF set can efficiently provide piecewise linear solutions for a variety of control systems. A few examples are included with pertinent figures and tables, and the findings are compared using current methodologies to verify the accuracy of the solution and the efficacy of the method being discussed.

articleTitle: An Explainable Educational Data Mining System for Predicting Student Academic Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Students' educational accomplishments are vital as they are a key indicator of their overall academic journey. This study proposes a Machine Learning (ML) enabled approach to categorize students' academic performance with the explainability of the proposed EDM system. We utilized standard ML models like Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Boosting models such as Gradient Boosting and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) for multi-class classification, where XGB outperforms other models with 83% accuracy, precision, and recall. The proposed EDM approach demonstrates superior performance compared to existing works, offering a more effective approach for anticipating and enhancing student academic outcomes. The explainability results demonstrate that changes in curriculum, courses, and the status of paying tuition fees can bring a positive result in the student's academic performance. Future research focuses on designing a recommendation system to help the students justify their current status and get personalized support to enhance academic performance in real time.

articleTitle: An Efficient Algorithm for Detecting Total Sleep Time from Electroencephalography Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Polysomnography (PSG), the gold standard for sleep analysis, is manually scored by sleep experts. The measurement of total sleep time (TST) from PSG is very important for diagnosing sleep related abnormalities. Manual scoring of TST is time consuming and vary among experts. This study aimed to develop an algorithm for automatically detecting the TST from single-channel electroencephalography (EEG) signals collected from overnight PSG recordings. The algorithm was developed and optimized using a development dataset of 41 EEG records and tested using a validation dataset of 46 EEG records. The designed algorithm took the raw EEG as input, and pre-processed it by filtering and removing the phase shift. The feature was extracted from each 30-second EEG epoch and classified each epoch as sleep or wake using an optimized threshold. TST was estimated by summing up these epochs classified as sleep. The estimated TST was compared to the standard annotation for performance evaluation. A good agreement was established between the algorithm and annotation using the Bland-Altman plot that indicated a very small mean bias of -0.16 hours with a narrow limit of agreement of -3.76 to 3.43 hours. Since the designed method outperformed the existing relevant studies, this algorithm can be effectively applied for the early diagnosis of sleep related disorders, especially sleep apnea.

articleTitle: Modified InceptionV3 Model for Brain Tumor Classification with Grad-CAM Explainability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: The unrestrained growth of an abnormal cell cluster is the distinguishing characteristic of a brain tumor, which poses a highly dangerous situation. Inaccurate diagnoses of brain tumors will make it more challenging for them to receive treatment on time and reduce a patient's chances of life. Accurate tumor diagnosis is crucial for improving patient survival rates in medical imaging. Accordingly, this paper offers a modified pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) model for accurate brain tumor classification. For this purpose, four distinct pre-trained CNN models: VGG16, InceptionV3, DenseNet121, and MobileNetV2 are utilized for primary classification. The top classification layers of these models are removed and replaced with additional layers for the modification task. This procedure leads to the generalization of the modified pre-trained CNN models. In addition, we have constructed a customized CNN model including softmax classification. Following the analysis, it is found that the suggested model, which is a modified version of InceptionV3,achieves an impressive accuracy of 99.16%. Other models also yielded acceptable results: the modified MobileNetV2, VGG16, DenseNet121, and the customized CNN achieved accuracy of 98.16%,92.52%,99.09%, and 95.19%, respectively. To improve the interpretability of the proposed model's output, we employed Grad-CAM to visually represent the regions of the images the proposed model focuses on.

articleTitle: Enhanced YOLOv9-Based Endangered Tiger Detection Framework for Wildlife Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Tiger conservation requires integrating diverse strategies, including preserving natural habitats, stringent anti-poaching efforts, and active community participation to ensure sustainable tiger population growth. The emergence of artificial intelligence presents an opportunity to enhance tiger surveillance through automated object detection. This paper introduces a robust, illumination-invariant framework that leverages Enlight-enGAN and the advanced YOLOv9c model for detecting Amur tigers. The fine-tuned YOLOv9c model, coupled with illumination enhancement techniques, achieves an impressive mAP50-95 score of 71.2% and an mAP50 score of 98.7% on the ATRW dataset. This approach significantly advances the state-of-the-art in tiger detection and highlights the potential of AI -driven solutions in wildlife conservation.

articleTitle: TranSenA: A Transformer-based Framework for Sentiment Analysis of Restaurant Reviews
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Sentiment analysis (SA) of restaurant reviews is pivotal in understanding customer experiences and preferences, allowing businesses to enhance service quality and customer satisfaction. This study presents an automatic framework that leverages transformer-based techniques for SA of restaurant reviews in Bengali. To underscore the importance of this research, a new Bengali Restaurant Review Dataset (BRRD) has been meticulously developed, featuring 11,004 labeled restaurant reviews categorized into positive, negative, and neutral. The SA tasks were performed using various ML, DL, and transformer-based models, including LR, RF, DT, SVM, AdaBoost, CNN, BiLSTM, CNN + BiLSTM, XLM-R, mBERT, and BanglaBERT. Experimental evaluations reveal that BanglaBERT achieved the highest weighted f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-score of 0.90, outperforming the other models used in this study.

articleTitle: COVID-19 Detection from Cough Sound Signal using Random Forest Learning of Deep Spectral Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: The COVID-19 epidemic and its subsequent rise have brought attention to the need for quick, precise, and reasonably priced testing techniques. Existing assays such as RT-PCR are slow and conditionally sensitive, which presents difficulties, particularly in low-resource settings. Researchers have shown that COVID-19 can be accurately detected by audio-based AI algorithms using cough sounds. In this work, a cough sound-based COVID-19 detection framework is presented. It utilizes a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) deep feature extractor from handcrafted spectral features and Random Forest classifier for classifying the healthy and Covid-19 subjects from cough sounds. The research considered the cough sound from two datasets named Coswara and Virufy emphasizing the generalization capability of the proposed framework. With the help of feature engineering, spectral features like Short-Term Fourier Transform (STFT), Mel Spectrogram, Mel Frequency Cepstrum Coefficient (MFCC), RMS Energy, Spectral Bandwidth, Zero Crossing Rate (ZCR), Spectral Centroid, and Spectral roll-off have been extracted which are further fed into a CNN based algorithm for extracting deep features. The deep features are more crucial for complex pattern analysis compared to the simple frequency domain analysis. Finally, the Random Forest model is used for classification tasks, which shows a predictive accuracy of 93% with robustness against data diversity. The proposed framework might be useful for smartphone-based COVID-19 detection applications.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a PCF-SPR Biosensor for Enhanced Blood Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: A novel biosensor incorporating photonic crystal fiber (PCF) and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was designed for the early detection of blood cancer cells. Finite element method simulation demonstrated a significant wavelength sensitivity of 10357.143 nm/RIU within the 2000–2400 nm spectral range. These findings suggest the potential of the PCF SPR sensor as a valuable diagnostic tool for blood cancer, offering enhanced sensitivity, cost-effectiveness and efficiency, thereby contributing to improved patient outcomes and early intervention.

articleTitle: Enhancing Bangla Language Text Recognition in OCR Using Levenshtein Distance and Character Grouping Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: One crucial technology for text digitization from image is optical character recognition (OCR). Character recognition in languages with complex scripts, like Bangla, is still difficult despite recent advancements. This research proposes an innovative approach to enhance OCR's Bangla text recognition capabilities. In order to improve recognition performance, OCR errors are efficiently corrected and performance is improved by first applying the Levenshtein distance measure. Experiments show a notable improvement, increasing the initial weighted F1-score of Tesseract OCR from 84.96% to 87.26%. In addition, a method of character grouping is demonstrated to address nuances specific to the Bangla script. Characters that share visual similarities are categorized into different groupings. Subsequently, priority is given to dictionary candidate words with characters that belong to the same class as those identified by OCR. Integrating the character grouping technique yields an astounding 90.92% F1-score.

articleTitle: Development of a System to Prioritize Sustainable Energy Solutions Utilizing Double-Stage Optimization Techniques: A Case Study of Rajshahi, Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This study examines the optimal renewable energy technology for evaluating the electrification system in Rajshahi, Bangladesh. A proposed approach integrates the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with the TOPSIS method to determine the optimal RET. The HOMER Pro simulation tool has been used to determine the best combination. The analysis considers solar-wind, biomass, wind, solar, solar-wind-battery, and hydro energy systems. Based on expert opinions and consensus, fifteen sub-criteria were selected across four key categories: economic, technical, socio-economic, and environmental. After the best optimization with HOMER Pro software, AHP determines the weights of these criteria, sensitivity analysis checks the robustness of the study and finally, TOPSIS ranks the RETs. The outputs disclose that the solar-wind-battery system emerges as the most favorable option, achieving the highest appraisal score among the evaluated alternatives. The sensitivity analysis confirms the ranking's consistency. This combined MCDM approach proves valuable for selecting RETs in Rajshahi. Therefore, these methods can be a useful tool for decision-making regarding renewable energy development in Rajshahi as well as any other locations in the country.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of MVDR Beamformer with Conventional Beamformer for the Efficient Interference Reduction by Null-Forming for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This paper offers the idea of a minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) beamformer in order to reduce interference by null-forming in an efficient way as compared with the conventional beamformer (CBF), and the research conveys the idea. The study is carried out by analyzing the radiation pattern of the CBF and MVDR beamformers for various numbers of interference power levels and inter-element spacing. The CBF and MVDR beamformers are tested to see how well they work in a number of different situations involving the source direction and interference signals. When it comes to eliminating interference, however, the MVDR beamformer has proven to be more accurate than the CBF. To further validate the MVDR beamformer's performance, this study demonstrates its simulation-based implementation in a phased array monostatic radar system.

articleTitle: A CMOS Instrumentation Amplifier for Photoacoustic Signal Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: The design of a low noise, high bandwidth, and high-speed instrumentation amplifier tuned for accurate measurement of photoacoustic signals in biomedical applications is presented. The designed amplifier's gain and bandwidth are tunable up to 54.3 dB and 166.12 kHz respectively. Besides, a gain-dependent high CMRR of up to 114.4 dB with at least 102 dB (-) and 67 dB (+) PSRR, along with only 40.88 nV/Hz input referred thermal noise and choice of 2 pF capacitive load make the amplifier immune to noisy environments. Additionally, the 2 pF capacitive load ensures a fast response of the instrumentation amplifier.

articleTitle: Prediction of Rainfall in Sylhet Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Rainfall significantly impacts lots of areas of human life, Including natural calamities for example landslides, floods, droughts, agriculture, etc. Floods are one of the most serious disasters especially for the rural communities of our country as Sylhet. The recent flood caused a lot of damage to Sylhet in 2022, including the destruction of safe housing and healthy food as well as numerous mortality from a need for adequate medical care. Accurate rainfall forecasts can be beneficial for agriculture, aviation, natural disasters, floods, construction, and transportation industries. This study's objective is to build the prediction and analysis of probability. Machine learning is one of the most popular techniques used for rain prediction and probability. Total 21390 day data in Sylhet Weather Forecast. Weather Forecasting Dataset collected from Bangladesh Rice Research Institute website. The dataset contains Climate data recorded on a daily basis from 1956 to 2014. We applied data preprocessing use with label encoders, feature scaling and standard scalars to improve data behavior and performance, we removed null values and extraneous items. With the preprocessed data. we have run some classification algorithms to predict Rain or no rain, rain in millimeters, and Rain Category. Among them, we got the best accuracy results from the Random Forest Algorithm and KNN. In the next, we implemented the formula of Naive Bayes probability to find Rain or no rain and Rain Categories probability.

articleTitle: Predicting Endotracheal Suctioning Activities Based On Skeletal Coordinates: A Novel Approach Combining Handcrafted Feature Engineering and Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Endotracheal Suctioning (ETS) is a critical procedure typically carried out to patients with artificial airways in intensive care units. It is an extremely delicate procedure requiring adequate expertise to minimize the risk of complication and ensure patient safety. Although numerous studies have applied machine learning techniques for the purpose of nurse-care activity recognition, little works focus specifically on endotracheal suctioning activity recognition. Utilizing a model proficient in categorizing endotracheal suctioning activities can serve as a valuable tool for evaluating nursing proficiency. In this paper we use skeletal coordinate data obtained from the 6th ABC Challenge (Activity Recognition of Nurse Training Activity) and apply machine learning techniques to predict activities associated with ETS. Following some data pre-processing steps including data smoothing, we extracted joint angles, velocity and several time-domain features and performed data augmentation. We split the data into training and test set and finally, we employed an ensemble model for classifying the ETS activities. The ensemble model yielded superior results than conventional machine learning approaches with an accuracy of 68% and a macro average f1-score of 71 %.

articleTitle: Retrieving Top K% Relevant Patterns for Relation Extraction in Bangla Using Distant Supervision
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Information extraction constitutes a piv-otal domain within natural language processing (NLP) aiming to distill structured insights-such as entity types and their relationships-from diverse textual sources. Relation extraction, a core task within this field, automates identifying and classifying relation-ships between entities mentioned in unstructured text. This paper explores distant supervision (DS) methods tailored for Bangla, addressing the linguistic nuances and challenges of data scarcity. DS leverages knowl-edge bases for automatic corpus labeling, although this can introduce noise. Our location mnemonics help reduce some noisy patterns related to location-based relations. Additionally, our proposed method retrieves the top K% relevant patterns using conflict scores which is further refined with probability scores. Setting K to 80% results in an impressive F1 score of 91 %, demonstrating the efficacy of our approach.

articleTitle: Design of a Quadruple Band Metamaterial Absorber for Sensing in the Terahertz Region
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This work proposed the design and analysis of a high performance quadruple band metamaterial absorber suitable for terahertz (THz) sensing applications. The unit cell of the structure is comprised of two concentric square metal rings placed on a polyimide substrate and a metal ground plane beneath them. The concept being considered here depends on the impedance matching between the absorber and the medium above it. The sensor can detect a wide range of refractive indices (1.0 - 1.6), covering most of the biosamples, and the use of multiband ensures high accuracy in the detection of analytes. The proposed design offers high sensing performance with a maximum sensitivity of 160, 240, 450, and 720 GHz/RIU and a maximum Q factor of 25.421, 26.738, 59.712, and 51.516, respectively, at its four resonant frequencies. The sensor is polarization insensitive which will have less complexity in the measurement setup. It is also capable of providing a maximum FOM of 8.421, 5.310, 14.803, and 14.145. The proposed structure's properties, including its high sensing performance, polarization insensitivity, and structural simplicity, contribute to its being an excellent candidate for THz biosensing applications.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of Area-Time Efficient Modular Multiplication over NIST Prime Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This research presents an efficient modular multipli-cation for elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) over NIST prime fields. The development of ECC processors that can perform modular multiplication while minimizing hardware utilization is a crucial need in cryptography and cybersecurity. The efficiency of modular multiplication is a key factor that directly impacts the overall performance of ECC processors. Achieving fast modular multiplication with low hardware usage involves optimizing the design of ECPs to balance computational speed, resource utilization, and resistance to side-channel attacks. Our proposed design aims to achieve higher performance with reduced power consumption. For performance evaluation, we synthesized our design on various FPGA platforms, including Virtex-7 and Virtex-6, using different NIST primes. The mostly used 256-bit modular multiplication device utilization is reduced greatly here, and we extend this work to higher bits, i.e., 384-bit and 521-bit NIST primes.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation of Group Operations for Elliptic Curve Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Group operations determine how efficiently elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) can operate. In this study, we propose efficient and optimized point addition (PA) and point doubling (PD) algorithms and hardware architectures to enhance ECC's efficiency and security. The repetitive use of PA and PD in scalar multiplication can significantly save area and time in designing ECC protocols, especially when these operations are implemented efficiently. We present a more area-time efficient design approach that consumes only 2681 slice registers with 5.495 μs latency for PA and 2309 slice registers with 4.961 μs latency for PD. The Xilinx 14.7 design tool is used to synthesize and analyze PA and PD architectures using VHDL. The Kintex-7 FPGA ‘7k70tfbg676-1’ model is used for the overall design. This design platform consumes minimal power, 0.079W, and can withstand high thermal margins of 74.9°C and 40.4W. Our proposed design achieves a lower area-delay product, with values of 0.015 for PA and 0.011 for PD, and maximizes throughput rates. The higher values of the figure of merit, 67.87 for PA and 87.29 for PD, indicate that the proposed design is highly efficient and optimized.

articleTitle: Optimizing EEG-based Microsleep Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Time and Frequency Domain Features Utilizing SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Microsleeps are short, involuntary episodes of sleep that can have serious safety implications, especially in high-risk occupations. This study investigated optimal features for detecting microsleeps using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. EEG data was collected from 15 participants using an 8- channel wearable headset. Six feature extraction techniques were evaluated: standard deviation, mean, and variance from the time domain; power spectral density, fast Fourier transform, and spectral centroid from the frequency domain. A Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier with RBF kernel was utilized to classify the extracted features. Performance was assessed using metrics including accuracy, specificity, precision, recall, and F1-score. Results showed that FFT achieved the highest overall performance, with 93.50% accuracy, 93.55% specificity, 93.88% precision, 93.49% recall, and 93.68% F1- score. Standard deviation was the next best performing feature. These findings suggest that frequency domain features, particularly FFT, showed high performance for effective microsleep detection from EEG signals utilizing SVM. This approach could potentially be applied to develop systems for monitoring and preventing microsleep in safety-critical environments.
