articleTitle: A Regularized LSTM Method for Detecting Fake News Articles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Nowadays, the rapid diffusion of fake news poses a significant problem, as it can spread misinformation and confusion. This paper aims to develop an advanced machine-learning solution for detecting fake news articles. Leveraging a comprehensive dataset of news articles, including 23,502 fake news articles and 21,417 accurate news articles, we implemented and evaluated three machine-learning models. Our dataset, curated from diverse sources, provides rich textual content categorized into title, text, subject, and Date features. These features are essential for training robust classification models to distinguish between fake and authentic news articles. The initial model employed a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, achieving an accuracy of 94%. The second model improved upon this by incorporating additional regularisation techniques and fine-tuning hyperparameters, resulting in a 97% accuracy. The final model combined the strengths of previous architectures with advanced optimization strategies, achieving a peak accuracy of 98%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in identifying fake news with high precision. Implementing these models showcases significant advancements in natural language processing and machine learning techniques, contributing valuable tools for combating misinformation. Our work highlights the potential for deploying such models in real-world applications, providing a reliable method for automated fake news detection and enhancing the credibility of news dissemination.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning Technique for Brain Tumor Classification from MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Brain cancer has the greatest death rate of any cancer, and it is difficult to classify tumors in medical imaging due to their aberrant proliferation of cells, forms, orientation, and location. Therefore, using computer-assisted methods is crucial to overcoming these limitations. Here, we proposed a model for classifying brain tumors from MRI images using deep transfer learning models. This work centers on three pre-trained models, specifically InceptionResNetV2, ResNet101V2, and MobileNetV2. We added extra layers after the base model output layer. From the InceptionResNetV2 model, we got the best accuracy with a low loss value. Our model's top validation accuracy was 98.86% and testing accuracy was 99.15%. Based on a comparison with different models, our proposed model has a high level of reliability in the early identification of brain tumors.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Plant Disease Detection Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Agriculture is becoming a significant business in Bangladesh due to the country's expanding population and rising food demands. Consequently, it is imperative to raise agricultural productivity. Among the important factors influencing lower agricultural yields are diseases caused by bacteria, fungi, and viruses. Techniques for detecting plant diseases can be used to control and prevent this. Since deep learning techniques primarily use plant data and provide very effective means of identifying plant ailments, they will be used for the diagnosis of plant diseases. Using deep learning and machine learning based on artificial intelligence (AI), the method offers a thorough assessment of all the methods used in plant disease detection. For our study, we have considered Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), MobileNetV2 and Inception V3techniques. Following preprocessing, the models receive 80% of the datasets for training purposes and the remaining 20% for testing. After the disease has been detected, performance analysis and model comparison are carried out. It is found that MobileNetV2 outperforms the other applied approaches, yielding an accuracy of 98.43 %.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of FACsSnI3 Perovskite Solar Cells: Variations in Electron Affinity and Defect Density with Different ETLs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of electron affinity and defect density on the performance of FACsSnI3- based perovskite solar cells using five different electron transport layers (ETLs): SnS2, PCBM, CdZnS, LBSO, and TiO2. The analysis was conducted through simulations using SCAPS 1D software, focusing on key performance metrics such as efficiency, fill factor (FF), short-circuit current density (Jsc), and open-circuit voltage (Voc). The results indicate that SnS2 and CdZnS provide superior performance with higher efficiencies and better stability across various defect densities. In contrast, PCBM shows the lowest efficiency due to its lower electron affinity and poor defect tolerance. The study highlights the significance of choosing appropriate ETLs to optimize the overall performance of perovskite solar cells, providing a pathway for future research and development in this field.

articleTitle: Enhancing Anomaly Detection in Chipless RFID Systems: A GAN-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative method for anomaly detection in frequency response data within chipless Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) systems, addressing the significant limitations of conventional approaches. By leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), the proposed technique generates synthetic data that closely approximates the normal distribution, thereby significantly enhancing anomaly detection accuracy. Unlike traditional methods that often struggle with the complex patterns inherent in such data, this approach excels in decoding these intricacies. The effectiveness of the method was validated through extensive experiments on real-world datasets, consistently demonstrating robustness in identifying both subtle and overt anomalies. The results highlight the potential of the proposed approach to substantially improve anomaly detection capabilities in sophisticated RFID systems, offering a promising solution to longstanding challenges in the field. This advancement suggests a shift towards more reliable and efficient monitoring methods. The findings indicate that applying GANs in this context not only refines detection accuracy but also extends the operational reliability of RFID technologies.

articleTitle: A New Approach for Detecting Sleep Arousal from Single-Channel EMG Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Sleep arousal is a brief waking that occurs while a person is asleep and usually occurs without conscious awareness. The muscle relaxation at the back of the throat causes the airway to narrow or close during breathing, leading to decreased oxygen levels in the blood. The brain responds to this by briefly waking the person to reopen the airway, which is known as sleep arousal. The study aims to develop an algorithm using single-channel electromyography (EMG) signals for accurately detecting arousal occurrences. The algorithm was designed in such a way that took single-channel EMG signal as the input and after rigorous automatic operation, the output was produced as the number of arousal and normal epochs. The algorithm was trained and tested using 30 and 20 whole-night EMG records. The sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of 90%, 98%, and 98% respectively were achieved from the testing dataset. The performance was much better than the other existing literature. This automatic approach of sleep arousal detection can significantly contribute to the process of sleep apnea diagnosis.

articleTitle: Study of Single Crystalline Silicon Growth on Graphene Using Density Functional Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Si-Graphene heterostructure holds significant potential for high-performance electronic devices of the next generation. To design promising devices the growth of Si atop graphene needs greater attention. Also, Si thinfilm with superior quality can be developed using this technology. However, attempts are limited to grow Si on graphene, and the films produced are of low quality. Applying the density functional theory, this study explores that it is possible to grow Si on graphene. An AlN interface layer is proposed to improve the Si quality to grow as a single crystalline. Our analysis shows that the films grown on the AlN-graphene layer possessed better qualities and stability than those grown on graphene due to weak van der Waals interaction. Moreover, the Si crystal quality improves dramatically with increasing number of Si bilayers.

articleTitle: Enhanced SDN Defense: Analysis of DDoS Attack Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Software defined network (SDN) is drawing attention to handling next-generation traffic through centralized management. However, the centralized aspect of the network makes it more vulnerable because the central controller might be targeted by malicious actors looking to interfere with network operations and data security. Typically, the SDN controller defense system uses machine learning (ML) techniques to inspect data from individual IP to detect distributed denial-of-service and intrusion attacks. As soon as an anomaly is detected, the system enables rapid response to mitigate attacks and ensure smooth system operations. In the accessed model, the CICDDoS-2019 public dataset is used to evaluate and compare the performance with various ML algorithms. Ultimately, an efficient mitigation approach is suggested and utilized for each detection method. The results suggest guaranteed detection rates and efficient throughput. Therefore, the multi-layer perceptron approach is suitable for the SDN defense system.

articleTitle: Detection of Voice Disorder Using Spectral and Statistical Audio Features and SVM-RBF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: The detection of voice disorders using voice signal processing and machine learning has emerged as a promising early diagnosis and treatment approach. This paper presents a machine learning-based automatic voice disorder detection framework extracting and selecting optimum features from voice audio signals. The practical challenge of class-imbalanced scenario of disorder and healthy voices data is addressed using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). Several features, i.e., Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), Chroma Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), zero crossing rate, root mean square, skewness, and kurtosis; have been studied in spectral and statistical domains. Finally, the optimum features are selected using the Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation (RFECV) technique to reduce the classifier model's complexity. A support vector machine (SVM) classifier with a Radial basis function kernel is developed, prioritizing simplicity and efficiency. The SVM model is trained and tested using the well-accepted VOICED database of PhysioNet Data Bank where the audio is captured using a smartphone. The performance of the overall framework shows an accuracy of 95% and 100% precision and specificity, demonstrating its resilience for precise evaluations and smartphone-based diagnosis applications.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Image-Based Abusive Bengali Memes Using Ensemble and Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: In the realm of internet communication, memes have emerged as a powerful means of expression, swiftly disseminating emotions and ideas. The ability to classify memes, particularly in languages with regional nuances such as Bengali, poses unique challenges. The primary question of this study addresses how to efficiently classify Bengali memes, given their diverse and context-specific nature. The motivation for this research stems from the growing significance of memes as a form of internet communication and the need for effective methods to categorize and understand them. This work presents here a computational model of classifying Bengali memes using convolutional neural networks. Convolutional neural networks have the potential to learn, adapt, and rearrange themselves. Along-side employing traditional machine learning models-Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression, and Random Forest for meme classification. The experiment illustrated a CNN model with Bi-LSTM layers is implemented, achieving a test accuracy of 69.49%. Additionally, Among the machine learning models, the Random Forest achieves the highest accuracy of 64%. Our study shows that this comparison between CNN-based and traditional models provides valuable insights for future research in meme analysis and content moderation.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of CMOS-Based Common Source and Cascode Amplifiers Using 90 nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: CMOS-based amplifiers are extensively utilized in modern electronics due to their efficiency in power consumption and ability to integrate densely. These amplifiers harness the complementary characteristics of NMOS and PMOS transistors to achieve high amplification and broad bandwidth. However, traditional CMOS amplifiers often exhibit lower gain due to factors such as suboptimal width-to-length ratios and improper biasing. This study investigates CMOS-based common source amplifiers and Cascode amplifiers using the Cadence Virtuoso environment with the Generic Process Design Kit 90 nm (gpdk090). The designs are configured with a 2.5 V DC source and utilize paired NMOS and PMOS transistors, each with a gate length of 100 nm. A thorough analysis encompassing transient, DC, and AC characteristics was performed for both types of CMOS amplifiers. The results indicate that the common source amplifier achieved a gain of 404, whereas the Cascode amplifier demonstrated a higher gain of 499. These findings validate the superior performance of the Cascode configuration in terms of amplification efficiency. The study underscores the robustness of these amplifier designs, affirming their suitability for integrated circuit development and analog circuit applications.

articleTitle: An IoT-Based Calculator for Body Mass Index Determination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This paper illustrates the creation of a portable Body Mass Index (BMI) calculator that uses ultrasonic sensors and load cells interfaced with a microcontroller to determine BMI automatically. The novelty of our system lies in its automation of real-time weight and height measurements, eliminating the need for manual input, and integrating data logging with cloud-based monitoring. Our system provides a sustainable and user-friendly solution for BMI determination, surpassing the drawbacks of manual approaches, even with load cell calibration and sensor alignment being intrinsically difficult problems. Ultrasonic sensors are used to detect height, and load cells are arranged in a Wheatstone bridge to measure weight. A microprocessor processes the data to compute BMI values. While the ultrasonic sensor determines height by timing the return of transmitted sound waves, the load cell determines weight by monitoring changes in electrical resistance under applied force. This automated, microcontroller-based BMI calculator encourages a healthy lifestyle and sensible weight management by being reasonably priced and flexible enough to work in a variety of settings, including isolated and resource-constrained locations. Our study aims to develop low-cost, effective BMI measurement equipment that can be used in a variety of scenarios. To ensure sustainability in terms of functionality and environmental effects, future work will focus on improving calibration techniques to increase accuracy and enable greater deployment. Our method seeks to enhance health monitoring and management in various communities by addressing the challenges of manual BMI estimates, particularly in resource-poor locations.

articleTitle: Recognition of Bengali Vowels from Auditory Evoked Potentials Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Audio evoked potentials, or AEPs, have recently gained popularity. It can be described as the EEG signal generated when a person is exposed to auditory stimuli. The human brain behaves differently when exposed to diverse sounds. It also produces a distinct hemodynamic activity pattern for speech sounds compared to non-speech sounds. This paper presents a system for capturing AEP. The proposed approach covers seven different Bengali vowels. A total of 208 sets of data were obtained from five different subjects. The various AEP signals were then filtered and pre-processed. Different features Power Spectral Density (PSD), Entropy, and Variance have been extracted from the preprocessed signal. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) has the highest accuracy (90.96 %) for PSD features. The dataset has been made public for future research purposes.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Miniaturized, Efficient Wideband THz Antenna for 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: A wideband, small-size inset-fed slotted rectangular THz antenna with a polyamide substrate has been designed and analyzed for 6G applications. The substrate measures 27.809×40×10 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, which is significantly smaller than known antennas currently in use. The antenna has an operating bandwidth of 1060 GHz, which spans 4.46 THz to 5.52 THz, and it resonates at 5.01 THz. The radiation efficiency, return loss, and maximum gain of the proposed THz antenna are 6.29 dB, 97.6%, and −61.97 dB, respectively. In terms of bandwidth, maximum gain, radiation efficiency, and return loss, the proposed THz antenna performs better. A high-frequency structure simulator (HFSS) platform is used to simulate the proposed model and estimate its performance for 6G communication.

articleTitle: Modeling the Sharing and Diffusion of Fake News in Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: The use of social media platforms has been gradually increasing and fake news spreading is becoming an alarming issue nowadays. The spreading of fake news means disseminating false, confusing, and spurious information which hurts families, communities etc. As a result, this issue has to be resolved sooner so that we can limit the spread of fake news in the virtual world. One needs to identify the fake news spreader to address this issue. In this research, we have tried to reveal the users who are most likely to share fake news as well as the spread prediction that shared pieces of fake news in the social network. We take into account the users' information, such as follower counts, like counts, and retweet counts along with users' topical interests on different topics as well as connection strength by considering the follower-following ratio. We also consider the complexity features, stylistic features, and psychological effects of news. Finally, we applied different machine-learning algorithms to evaluate the performance of the proposed model. Our observation is that the probability of spreading a piece of news shared by users having more followers as well as more likes and retweet counts (aka influential users) is higher compared with other users.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual Band Microstrip Patch Antenna for 5G mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: In today's wireless communication era, 5G technology is crucial for fast and secure data exchange. This paper explores the pivotal role of the 28.2 GHz and 37.11 GHz frequency bands in advancing 5G applications, addressing the essential need for enhanced data speeds, reduced latency, and superior connectivity in emerging wireless networks. The proposed antenna, with dimensions of 7×7.5×0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, utilizes a Rogers RO4350 (lossy) substrate with a dielectric constant (∊<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) of 3.66 and a thickness of 0.8 mm. It features a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 2.54 GHz and 3.06 GHz at 28.2 GHz (27.02 GHz - 29.56 GHz) and 37.11 GHz (35.15 GHz - 38.21 GHz). The antenna achieves -26 dB return loss at 37.11 GHz and -24 dB at 28.2 GHz, with gains of 4.38 dBi and 6.9 dBi, respectively. Radiation efficiency reaches 67% at 28.2 GHz and exceeds 83% at 37.11 GHz while maintaining the VSWR condition. Its compact size and outstanding performance make this antenna a promising option for future 5G mobile communication technologies.

articleTitle: SwiftCNN: A Deep Learning Model for B-ALL Diagnosis and Subtype Classification from Blood Smear Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: The most advanced methods available today are convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which are frequently used for image categorization tasks. This article uses sophisticated neural network models to explore the categorization of peripheral blood smear pictures for B-ALL diagnosis and its subtypes. We introduce a method for classifying images using a modified VGG19 model. Images are pre-processed at first before being input into the multi-class classification algorithms. We discovered throughout this study that the suggested methods improve model performance. Our study focused on two types of images: benign and malignant, as well as three subtypes of malignant lymphoblasts: Early Pre-B, Pre-B, and Pro-B ALL. The model has a validation loss of 0.1499 and an accuracy of 94.63%, whereas its training loss is 0.1127 and 96.97%, respectively. These findings demonstrate how well the VGG19-based model performs in terms of categorization.

articleTitle: Breaking Efficiency Barriers: Triple Absorber Layer Solar Cells with Over 36% Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This research looks into the potential of solar cells with three absorber layers: CsGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, FACsSnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, and Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is used as the electron transport layer (ETL), and Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O is used as the hole transport layer (HTL). Using SCAPS-1D simulations, we varied parameters such as defect density and doping density to optimize power conversion efficiency (PCE). The tri-layer configuration was more efficient than the bilayer (28.65% PCE) and single-layer (25.73% PCE) devices, with a PCE of over 36%. Key findings revealed that CsGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and FACsSnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> exhibit high defect tolerance, while Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is sensitive to defects, impacting its PCE and other performance metrics. When the right amount of doping was used, FACsSnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> worked much better, especially when it came to open-circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf>) and PCE. Temperature variations showed a decline in PCE, highlighting the need for effective thermal management. This research underscores the advantages of multi-layer architectures in improving photovoltaic performance and stability.

articleTitle: PCA-Enhanced Deep Learning Method for Network Intrusion Detection: A Multi-Label Classification Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) are a significant advance in addressing the ever-changing nature of information systems and preventing potential cyber-attacks. The complexity and volume of network traffic is making traditional methods ineffective. To addressing these challenges, a PCA-enhanced deep learning method is proposed for network intrusion detection incorporating multi label classification. By using Principle Component Analysis (PCA), reduces the high-dimensionality of network features that is more efficient for deep learning model training. This integration not only speeds up the training process but also enhances the models' generalization capabilities. Applying the proposed model to CSE-CIC-IDS2018 dataset, a remarkable 99.92% accuracy is achieved, which is a significant improvement in both detection accuracy and computational efficiency. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the PCA-Enhanced DL technique in real-world network contexts.

articleTitle: Precision Navigation: Dual Band GPS Receiver with Phased Array Technology and Directional Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: The increasing reliance on GPS for both military and civilian applications has emphasized the need for enhanced interference rejection and signal accuracy, particularly in environments with high levels of noise and jamming. This paper presents the design and simulation of a dual-band GPS receiver utilizing phased array technology and a directional antenna for precision navigation. The system is designed to dynamically steer beams toward GPS satellites while pointing nulls at interference sources. The phased array antenna operates at the L1 (1.5754 GHz) and L2 (1.2276 GHz) GPS frequencies and uses beamforming techniques to enhance signal reception. The system's performance is evaluated using 100 randomly generated data frames under various noise conditions, demonstrating a robust signal recovery with a low bit error rate (BER) of 0.004 at an SNR of −10 dB. Trilateration is used to calculate the GPS receiver's position, showing minor discrepancies compared to ground truth values due to clock precision limits in MATLAB. The results indicate that the proposed receiver design can significantly improve navigation accuracy and resilience against jamming. Future work will focus on hardware implementation and real-world testing to validate the system's performance in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: SPEI Based Drought Prediction and Validation Using Machine Learning Algorithm in Bangladesh from 1981 to 2017
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: A natural event known as a drought is defined by a long period of insufficient rainfall and limited access to water supplies, which means there isn't enough water for many uses, including agriculture, industry and domestic consumption. The Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) is a frequently utilized indicator in drought monitoring. In this work, from 1981 to 2017, temporal variation at Ishwardi upazila was used to evaluate and analyze the SPEI's performance at 1, 3, 6 and 12-month timeframes. An analysis is carried out to see how well machine learning approach such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random-Forest (RF), Decision-Tree (DT), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) work in forecasting drought conditions. The prediction outcomes of all five techniques were assessed using four performance measures: the Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Nash-Sutcliffe Model Efficiency Coefficient (NSE). The proposed methods provided good results and can serve as a quick decision-making tool for water management.

articleTitle: Optimizing K-Means for the Deployment of UAV-Assisted Wireless Networks: A Parametric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Presently, wireless communications have become a very popular and technologically advanced sector in the realm of telecommunications. Due to their comparatively lower cost and higher mobility, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV s) are now being considered as substitutes for traditional terrestrial base stations to provide coverage in areas without or lacking communication infrastructure. However, to make the use of UAV s as “flying base stations” a reality, a lot of challenges ahead to handle efficiently. One of the challenges is the positioning of multiple UAVs. The k-means clustering algorithm is exploited for UAV deployment. However, the impact of various parameters of k-means algorithm on the performance of UAV-assisted networks is yet to be investigated. In this paper, we investigate the impact considering various distance calculation methods, initial centroid determination methods, and so on. Through simulations, we find that the network performance varies significantly with the parameters. For a larger number of UAVs (12 or more), the impact of distance calculation and initial centroid position is significant. Furthermore, user throughput and satisfaction ratio are also affected. The k-means++ and sample method for initial centroid selection outperform other methods for average user throughput and user satisfaction ratio, respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel CNN Architecture for Alzheimer's Disease Classification Using MRI Images: Comparison with Traditional Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Automated medical image processing has significantly improved with recent advances in deep learning and imaging technologies, particularly in the area of neuroimaging-based Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis. Although various imaging modalities are available for individual patients, there is still a lack of research on the creation of multi-modal models that incorporate different modalities. AD is a neurological condition that worsens with time and affects daily activities. It affects memory, cognition, and behavior. AD cannot be cured, but it can be slowed down in its progression and quality of life enhanced with early care. Medical research is using machine learning (ML) more and more to diagnose and track diseases. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) can be used to detect AD, although it is still challenging to spot subtle changes in the brain in the early stages of the illness. In order to categorize four classes associated with AD symptoms Mild Demented (L-1), Very Mild Demented (L-2), Non-Demented (L-3), and Moderate Demented (L-4) we present a novel CNN architecture in this study. In order to identify the best accurate model, we also evaluate the performance of six ML algorithms. We trained and tested our proposed technique on the DATASET, which consists of 6400 MRI images and is publicly available on Kaggle database. Our results demonstrate that the proposed CNN model outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods with an accuracy of 98.7% and an F1-score of 98.9%. The most effective machine learning model that was looked at was Linear Regression (LR), which had an accuracy of 84.1% and an F1-score of 83.7%.

articleTitle: Achieving 40.34% Efficiency in KGeCl3 Solar Cells with Ag2S ETL and Cu2O HTL via SCAPS 1D Simulation Optimisation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on enhancing the efficiency of KGeC1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based perovskite solar cells (PSCs) using Ag2S as a ETL and Cu2o as an HTL through SCAPS 1D simulation optimization. The study investigates how several characteristics, such as material thickness, doping concentration, and defect density, affect important performance indicators such as Power conversion efficiency (PCE), open -circuit voltage (Voc), fill factor (FF), and short-circuit current density (Jsc). The optimized structure achieved a remarkable PCE of 40.34%, attributed to a balanced optimization of material thickness and defect management. The findings indicate that increased thickness enhances J sc and PCE initially but adversely affects FF and Voc. Additionally, optimizing the doping concentration significantly improves the overall performance by enhancing charge transport and reducing recombination. This study highlights the great efficiency that KGeC13 PSCs can achieve and offers ideas for future solar technology development and optimization.

articleTitle: LVQE: Laparoscopic Video Quality Enhancement Using GAN-Based Smoke Elimination Guided by an Embedded Dark Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Inthis study, a technique for effectively removing smoke from laparoscopic video recordings-which are often negatively impacted during surgeries-using an image-to-image generative adversarial network (GAN) with a built-in guide mask derived from the dark channel is presented. Smoke from tissue dissection tools can obstruct the surgeon's view and introduce errors into computer vision-based systems employed for clinical navigation. The GAN addresses this issue by eliminating noise while maintaining perceptually satisfactory image quality. Using the Laparoscopic Video Quality (LVQ) evaluation dataset, the method is trained and assessed. The section on experimental results provides qualitative examples demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach. With a larger, more diverse dataset for training and validation, further improvements are anticipated. The proposed technique generated smoke-free images and videos, surpassing previous methods.

articleTitle: A Sustainable RF-Based Wireless Power Transfer System for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This research investigates the transformative capabilities of wireless power transfer (WPT) in the context of medical devices. It presents several advantages, including increased convenience, diminished patient discomfort, and prolonged battery longevity when compared to conventional wired systems. By leveraging ambient RF signals, WPT eliminates the battery or cable demand, strengthening safety measures for patients and device reliability. The paper introduces a non-linear diode model designed to accurately simulate diode behavior, determines the input impedance for optimal matching, and develops a network that aligns impedance to enhance power transfer efficiency. Simulations assess the circuit's performance, with an RF-to-DC conversion effectiveness of 88.109%. The integrated rectifier, when combined with the antenna, can convert electromagnetic waves into DC power. This has promising applications in pace-makers, neurostimulators, and drug delivery systems, potentially revolutionizing energy solutions for implantable medical devices. efficiently.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Compact Wideband Metamaterial Absorber for Radar and Satellite Communications at Ku and K Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Metamaterial absorbers (MAs) are widely recognized for their near-unity absorption and ultrathin structure but typically be in distress from narrow bandwidth as a result of their resonance-based design. The goal of this research work is aimed at increasing the bandwidth of MAs while keeping them relatively small and easy to fabricate. We present a new MA design consisting of three consecutive layers: a copper ground plane, an FR4 dielectric substrate, & a double circle arrangement serving as the frequency selective surface (FSS). The suggested MA achieves a wideband absorption with a -10 dB BW of 13.63 GHz, extending from 13.86 GHz to 27.49 GHz, and a full width at half maximum (FWHM) BW of 15.42 GHz, according to simulation results using CST Studio. The simulation results reveal three distinct absorption peaks centered at 14.79 GHz, 19.73 GHz, and 24.65 GHz, with corresponding absorptivity values of 99.72%, 99.93%, and 99.92%. These exceptional absorption levels underscore the proposed design's efficacy in achieving near-perfect absorption at multiple frequencies, while also demonstrating a significant enhancement in broadband absorption performance. For applications needing wideband MAs with low structural complexity and good absorption efficiency, our study provides a potential answer.

articleTitle: Advancing Wearable Electronics via Shoe-Integrated Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This research explores the viability of utilizing human locomotion as a renewable energy source through piezo- electric energy harvesting. By embedding piezoelectric transducers within footwear, mechanical energy generated during movement can be effectively converted into electrical energy. A comprehensive power management circuit, including a battery, rectifier, and DC-DC converter, is proposed to optimize energy capture and storage. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in energy harvesting efficiency through strategic placement and sizing of the piezoelectric transducer within the shoe soles. These findings underscore the potential of this method for powering wearable electronics, advancing the development of sustainable, self-powered devices. Moreover, this approach extends the application of piezoelectric energy harvesting beyond traditional power sources, facilitating the creation of self-sustaining wearable sensors and devices, with potential applications in fields such as rehabilitation and sports science.

articleTitle: Detection of DDoS Attack: A Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks are a common and increasing threat to online services, targeting multiple layers of the OSI model. As communication technology advances, these attacks are getting more frequent and complicated, making detection and protection more challenging. Therefore, the need to study DDoS attack detection is growing. This paper evaluated multiple machine learning models for detecting DDoS attacks using binary classifications. We have used nine machine learning models for binary classification namely Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Gaussian Naïve Bayes, Extra Trees, AdaBoost, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression, and Multilayer Perceptron. Besides, we have selected the KDDCup99 dataset for this research. The dimensions of data determine a detection system's usefulness, consequently, feature selection and preprocessing are used to reduce the dataset's dimensionality, which minimizes the mathematical complexity. The evaluation of models is based on the accuracy, recall, precision, f1-score, false alarm rate, false positive ratio, false negative ratio, and error rate of datasets. Finally, using these evaluation criteria, we have compared the performance of the machine learning models and achieved the best results in binary classification using the XGBoost model with the highest accuracy (99.98%), precision (99.97%), recall (99.96%), f1-score (99.97%), and lowest false alarm rate (0.01 %), error rate (0.02<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), false positive ratio (0.03 %), and false negative ratio (0.03 %).

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques for Brain Stroke Analysis and Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Brain strokes a major contributor to global mortality and morbidity requires prompt prediction and intervention to reduce its impact. The study explores the practice of machine learning techniques for predicting brain strokes with the goal of improving early detection and preventive strategies. Utilizing a comprehensive dataset that includes demographic, lifestyle, and medical factors this study employs various machine learning systems such as logistic regression, random forest, decision tree, K-nearest neighbors, AdaBoost, XGBoost, and voting classifiers to develop predictive models. Feature ranking techniques are applied to detect the most significant variables which causes the incidence of stroke. The analysis incorporates preprocessing steps including data normalization, cleaning and managing missing values to determine the quality of the input data. Performance metrics including F1-score, recall, accuracy and precision are applied to measure the proficiency of the established models. Decision tree, XGBoost and voting classifier are showing best performance in this study with a similar accuracy of 96%. Additionally, this study contributes to build up a stacking model which achieved higher performance with an accuracy of 97%.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of IoT-Based Manhole Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Urban drainage and sewage systems are vital for public health and environmental sustainability. However, traditional maintenance methods often struggle with the complexities of modern infrastructure, leading to inefficiencies and safety risks. This paper presents a novel IoT-Based Manhole Management System (MMS) designed to revolutionize infrastructure management through proactive monitoring and maintenance. The MMS employs a combination of sensor networks, wireless communication, and data analytics to provide real-time monitoring and predictive maintenance capabilities. The study also evaluates the use of electro-mechanical probes for effective manhole cleaning, emphasizing their ability to precisely remove obstructions and adapt to various cleaning scenarios. Experimental models and literature reviews confirm the effectiveness and cost-efficiency of these advanced strategies. By integrating IoT technology with electro-mechanical probes, the research offers a comprehensive, safer, and more efficient approach to urban drainage system maintenance, contributing to improved infrastructure management and sustainability.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity through Genetic Algorithm-Based Phishing Website Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Cybercriminals design false webpages in an attempt to trick people into disclosing private information, such as passwords and credit card numbers. Strong cybersecurity measures are desperately needed, as phishing attacks are becoming more and more sophisticated. To improve cybersecurity, this study investigates the use of genetic algorithms for phishing website detection. We have used three real-world phishing website datasets to implement our work. Additionally, a thorough methodology that includes feature selection, data preprocessing, and the iterative process of the genetic algorithm is employed. This work proposes a hybrid-based method for phishing identification based on the website's URL that combines genetic and machine learning methods. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated by the results, which also show its adaptability, relative advantages over conventional methods, and promising generalizability. By shedding light on the useful applications of genetic algorithms for phishing detection, the study advances the field of cybersecurity. The final model proposed in this work has a 99.99% accuracy rate on the test set.

articleTitle: Enhancing Healthcare Precision: Utilizing Machine Learning for Accurate Patient Age Group Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Because machine learning (ML) can forecast age properly, it presents a substantial advantage in the dynamic field of healthcare when it comes to medical research, personalized therapies, and public health management. This paper uses a full machine learning technique to predict the patient age groups. It makes use of a dataset that includes a variety of attributes, including blood glucose, gender, physical activity, BMI, diabetes status, and insulin levels. Several supervised learning algorithms were applied, including Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM, Logistic Regression, and KNN. Maximum accuracy for the XGBoost algorithm was 97.2%, while for Random Forest, it was 94.2%. The findings show that machine learning significantly increases the accuracy of age prediction, supporting tailored treatments and preventative health care actions. By utilizing data-driven insights, this finding marks a paradigm change in precision medicine, transforming the delivery of health care and encouraging a more health-conscious population.

articleTitle: Cat-CNN: Human Eye Cataract Detection from Color Fundus Photograph with Deep CNN with Optimized Cascaded Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Cataracts are clouding of the lens in the eye, leading to loss of vision that can progress to blindness if not treated. This paper proposed a new method for automatic cataract detection using color fundus images and deep learning methods. A dataset of 1,105 color fundus images labeled by expert ophthalmologists was used in this process. We used seven pretrained CNNs (DenseNet121, EfficientNetB0, MobileNetV2, InceptionV3, Xception, ResNet50, VGG16, and VGG19) for feature extraction before reducing the extracted features using PCA. We used the following combination of machine learning classifiers: SVC, RF, Decision Tree, Gaussian Naive Bayes, XGBoost, K-Nearest Neighbors, and Logistic Regression. For evaluating the models' performance, we used accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and computational efficiency. For all metrics, MobileNetV2with Random Forest achieved perfect scores: 100% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, with an average processing time of 669 ms ± 28.8 ms. Thus, it can be applied in real-time applications. EfficientNetB0 with SVC gave an average accuracy of 87.33%, with the rest of the precision and recall metrics above 86%. Then, ResNet50, VGG16, and VGG19 followed with high accuracies between the range of 89.64% to 90.50%. It systemizes the proper choice of architectures of CNNs and classifiers, making the system both accurate and computationally efficient. Future work will include augmentation of the dataset, real-time support in the clinical setting, and advanced techniques for image preprocessing, generative adversarial networks. In addition, the development of an automated annotation tool, improvement of explainable AI, will further improve the deployment of robust AI systems in early diagnosis of cataracts, enhancing the outcome for patients.

articleTitle: Detection of Carbonated Beverages using a PCF SPR Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: A Photonic Crystal Fiber (PCF) Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) sensor has been proposed in this work. The sensor is designed for detecting the refractive index of carbonated beverages, such as Coca-Cola, Pepsi, 7UP, Sprite, Fanta, Mountain Dew, beer, stout, Canada Dry, and Schweppes. These beverages are widely consumed for their effervescence and refreshing taste. Ensuring their quality is crucial due to variations in alcohol content, sugar content, water mixture, aging process, and additional ingredients. The sensor, designed with a circular gold layer coating over a PCF with a symmetrical structure, facilitates the SPR phenomenon. Numerical exploration using the finite element method revealed a maximum amplitude sensitivity of 787 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>and a maximum wavelength sensitivity of 33,333.3 nm/RIU, with a wavelength sensitivity resolution of 3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>RIU and a high figure of merit of 555.56 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, confirming the sensor's superior performance. Demonstrating exceptional sensitivity, the sensor offers a costeffective and time-saving alternative to existing methods, also applicable in security settings such as airports and border checkpoints for detecting illegal substances. This study highlights the sensor's potential in ensuring the quality of carbonate beverages by providing valuable insights into their composition and authenticity, as well as enhancing security measures against illegal drug supply.

articleTitle: BDNEWS: Advance Bengali Sensitivity Corpus and Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: The development of natural language processing has been facilitated by introducing numerous high-quality datasets and cutting-edge methodologies. Downstream NLP tasks, including sentiment analysis, are essential for comprehending the context and emotional condition of users. Nonetheless, a comprehensive understanding of the broader aspects of text context remains scarce. To address this gap, we introduce a large-scale dataset BDNEWS that encompasses three dimensions of sensitivity: Worldwide, Countrywise, and Personal which are further categorized into two states-Positive and Negative-resulting in a total of six distinct sentiment categories. We manually curated this dataset from various local Bengali online news portals, comprising 6,989 instances. Additionally, to obtain more effective contextual embeddings, we utilized unsupervised techniques such as FastText and Word2Vec, which were employed to train a bespoke Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) model for precise sensitivity classification. FastText consistently surpasses Word2Vec in all metrics, illustrating its superiority in encapsulating the intricacies of Bengali language semantics. FastText achieves a maximum accuracy of 0.795 together with a recall score of 0.79 and a precision of 0.80. Moreover, its capacity to record sequential dependencies in text considerably improves the sensitivity prediction accuracy. These results give important new perspectives for sensitivity prediction in Bengali language applications and guide the next studies in this field.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Hybrid AC/DC Microgrids with Integrated Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This study examines the operational efficiency and stability of a hybrid-AC/DC microgrid integrated with renewable energy sources, addressing the need for sustainable power systems. Using the IEEE 14-bus system simulated in MATLAB/Simulink, it assesses microgrid performance under various load conditions, focusing on energy distribution and power quality. The research hypothesizes that advanced energy storage systems within microgrids smooth demand peaks, maintaining voltage stability between 0.9pu and 1pu, and Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) consistently below 5%. Analysis includes active and reactive power distributions, demand profiles, power losses, power factors, voltage levels, and harmonic distortions. Results show the hybrid microgrid maintains operational stability and efficiently manages power, with minor power quality variations during peak demand. Significant power losses were observed in low-voltage bus lines, especially lines 2 and 4, peaking at nearly 1.8kW/phase. This study offers valuable insights for designing efficient power systems, highlighting the importance of hybrid-microgrids in sustainable energy infrastructures.

articleTitle: Optimizing Round Robin Scheduling with DBSCAN Clustering and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: In the intricate realm of operating systems, scheduling algorithms play a pivotal role in resource allocation and process completion, directly impacting overall system performance. The quest for an efficient and optimized scheduling algorithm is perpetual in the pursuit of optimal operating system utilization. The Round Robin algorithm, known for its robust time-sharing methodology, emerges as a stalwart in the scheduling context. Its versatility spans various domains, making it a preferred choice in both general-purpose computing environments and real-time systems. This study aims to elevate the performance of the Round Robin algorithm in terms of average waiting time and number of context switches without altering its core algorithmic structure. A novel approach is proposed, utilizing DBSCAN to group related processes and determine a more accurate and efficient time quantum. Departing from the conventional practice of using a single time quantum for the entire schedule, we divide the schedule into groups. The optimal time quantum for each group is derived through machine learning and deep learning algorithms, leveraging rigorous features extracted from the schedule. Notably, the LSTM model emerges as the top performer, achieving an impressive 97% accuracy. The proposed modified version consistently outshines its traditional counterpart. In 92% of cases, the modified version demonstrates superior performance in average waiting time while achieving a 96.5% improvement in context switching. Considering both metrics, the modified version showcases a notable enhancement in 87.8% of cases. This holistic assessment unveils a 5% reduction in average waiting time and a substantial 15% decrease in context switching, signifying a meaningful advancement in overall system performance.

articleTitle: Shallow Feature Based Image-Text Retrieval Using Kernel Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Image-text retrieval has become more popular day-by-day due to its huge application on Facebook, YouTube, Google, LinkedIn, Twitter, etc. It is a cross-modal retrieval system considered a multi-class problem, which presents a challenging task in computer vision. Finding an appropriate combination of feature extraction and classification models is necessary to solve this multi-class problem effectively. This paper proposes a shallow feature-based cross-modal information retrieval system. Specifically, the scale-invariant feature transform (SIFT) is utilized as a shallow feature descriptor and the kernel extreme learning machine (KELM) is adopted as the classification model. Semantic matching (SM), correlation matching (CM), and semantic correlation matching (SCM) are applied in the matching strategy. The publicly available Wiki database is used for model learning. The mean average precision (mAP) is calculated as a statistical measure for each matching strategy, utilizing various distance metrics. The experimental results demonstrate that KELM achieves the highest mAP for SM, using a centered correlation measure, outperforming other matching strategies and statistical measures. Additionally, the results reveal that the SIFT feature-based KELM combination performs better than other competitive shallow feature-based approaches.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Brain Tumour Classification with CNN on MRI Scans
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: The process of classifying brain tumors using MRI data is difficult to do accurately. The challenges and limitations of manual analysis in treatments can be overcome by implementing Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems for categorizing brain tumors. This study assesses the performance of five well-known Transfer Learning CNN architectures - VGG19, VGG16, GoogleNet, ResNet-50, and DenseNet-121 - using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans. The main goal is to classify brain malignancies into four groups: no tumor, pituitary, meningioma, and glioma. The focus of this research for the classification task was on data preparation, training on preprocessed data, and comparing each model using evaluation metrics such as f1-score, accuracy, recall, and precision. Following preprocessing and training, the evaluation of the five CNN models revealed promising results for the VGG models, with both VGG19 and VGG16 achieving an accuracy score of 97%. This study indicates that among the base variants of Transfer Learning models, VGG19 and VGG16 are well-suited for classifying different types of brain tumors.

articleTitle: CyHy: A Centrality-aware Hybrid Caching Strategy in Information-centric Networking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: Network functionality has to be moved from the central server to the nearby user due to the recent explosion in multimedia applications' volume, worldwide accessibility, and rapid development. Inversely, typical Internet communications are inefficient as their main purpose is the transfer of data between hosts. As a result, a content-oriented networking paradigm known as information-centric networking (ICN) has surfaced. Researchers are trying to resolve implementation issues as ICN continues to develop. Allocating the space among cache-enabled nodes to maximize their benefits is a significantly difficult task because ICN has limited caching capability. In this work, a centrality-aware hybrid caching (CyHy) scheme has been proposed where cache storage distribution and content caching selection are made based on node relevance rather than uniformly dividing space among nodes. As node centrality metrics have a significant impact on caching decisions, we considered degree centrality which provides a local view, and betweenness centrality which provides a global view to find the important nodes in the network. Certain adjustments are suggested to the request packet and data packet structures to accommodate the proposed caching strategy. Finally, two real-world internet topologies are used for extensive modeling, and the results are compared with other standard caching techniques. The results of the simulation demonstrate that suggested caching outperforms others in terms of caching hit ratio, latency, and link load.

articleTitle: Enhancing Urban Traffic Management with Real-Time Computer Vision and AI: A Smart Traffic Signal System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: This research presents the development and deployment of a smart traffic signal system utilizing computer vision technology to optimize traffic management. Employing a pretrained YOLO model and Python's OpenCV library, the system achieves real-time vehicle and lane detection, facilitating dynamic adjustments to traffic signals based on actual traffic conditions. Key features include multi-lane vehicle counting, emergency vehicle prioritization, and the deployment of motorized traffic barriers, which reduce human intervention and streamline traffic flow. The system incorporates an optimization algorithm that efficiently manages lane availability based on traffic data, aiding in the reduction of road congestion. Both simulation and realworld testing have been conducted to validate the system's effectiveness in enhancing road safety and managing congestion. Additionally, the study explores the scalability of the solution to larger urban environments and addresses various technical challenges faced during implementation.

articleTitle: The Information Bottleneck Method in Deep Learning: Principles, Applications and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON)
abstract: The Information Bottleneck (IB) method provides a theoretical framework for balancing complexity and accuracy in machine learning models by compressing input data while retaining relevant information. This paper presents a compre-hensive review of the applications of the IB method in deep learning, focusing on its ability to enhance learning efficiency, generalization, and adversarial robustness. Variations like the Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) are also explored for their success in improving neural network performance. Notably, the VIB method performed superior on the MNIST dataset, outperforming conventional regularization techniques such as dropout and confidence penalty. In addition to achieving better generalization, the VIB model demonstrates greater resilience to adversarial attacks, requiring more substantial input mod-ifications to mislead the model. However, significant challenges remain, including optimization complexities and scalability issues in large data sets. This paper also identifies future research di-rections that aim to address these limitations, such as developing more scalable IB algorithms and enhancing adversarial defense mechanisms, to fully realize the potential of IB-based learning models.
